use: why something happens, at the scale of molecules
request: Why does ice float? Show the molecules.
intent: A curious viewer wants the molecular reason.
goal: The viewer knows ice's open lattice takes more room than liquid water, so ice is less dense and floats.
promise: Ice breaks a rule almost every solid follows.
arc: An ice cube floating, tumbling molecules, a lattice locking into hexagons, the open space compared.

events.text: Almost every solid sinks in its own liquid. Ice floats. Why?
In liquid water, molecules tumble close together.
events.knows: Liquid molecules are close and moving.

events.text: As water freezes, hydrogen bonds lock each molecule to four neighbors, in an open hexagon pattern.
events.knows: Ice is an open hexagonal lattice, four bonds each.

holds.does: the lattice holds still, its open middle visible

phases.why: molecules lock one bond at a time

events.text: That open lattice takes more room than the liquid, so ice is about nine percent less dense, and it floats.
events.knows: More room, about 9% less dense, so it floats.
events.look: the lattice beside the liquid, taking more room

measure.derived: Derived once from the request, intent and audience; thresholds not named here take the defaults in bench/lib/settings.ts. Read sizes scale with how wide the frame looks: a classroom or meeting screen from the back looks narrower than a phone at arm's length, a laptop at a desk wider. A hold listed as still is one the plan asks to wait without motion.

quiz.a: Its open hexagonal lattice takes more room than liquid water, so it is less dense.

quiz.q: How many neighbors does each molecule bond to in ice?
How much less dense is ice than water?
How did the molecules in the liquid look different from those in ice?
quiz.a: In the liquid they tumbled close together; in ice they were locked in an open hexagon pattern with space in the middle.

quiz.q: At the start, was the ice above or below the water surface?
quiz.a: Floating, with part above the water.

quiz.q: Were the molecules locked in all at once or one bond at a time?
While the lattice held still, what was visible in its middle?
